sights.address: Golden Gate Bridge, San Francisco, CA 94129
sights.w: The 1937 Art Deco suspension span in International Orange is SF's defining icon; the free Welcome Center and south vista point at Strauss Plaza sit at the city end for the classic view and a walk across the deck.
sights.k: Welcome Center open daily 9am-5pm; walkway free, southbound toll on drivers only.

sights.w: The former federal penitentiary in the middle of the bay, now a Golden Gate NRA site with the audio-guided cellhouse tour, gardens and the 1969 occupation history; ferries depart Pier 33 Alcatraz Landing.
sights.k: Book the City Experiences ferry well ahead - tickets sell out weeks out. A short dock repair briefly closed the island in April 2026; normal service resumed.

sights.address: Powell Street cable car turnaround, Powell St & Market St, San Francisco, CA 94102
sights.w: The world's last manually operated cable-car system, running since 1873; the Powell-Hyde and Powell-Mason lines climb Nob and Russian hills from the Powell/Market turnaround down to Fisherman's Wharf.
sights.k: A sheave-rehab project (Feb-Jun 2026) causes occasional segment closures with bus shuttles; at least one line stays running.

sights.w: Free museum inside the still-working Nob Hill powerhouse, where you can watch the giant sheaves and cables that haul every cable car in the city, plus antique cars and exhibits.
The 1898 Beaux-Arts ferry terminal with its landmark clock tower, reborn as a food hall of local artisans; the Tuesday/Thursday/Saturday farmers' market on the plaza is one of the country's best.

sights.address: Jefferson St & Taylor St, San Francisco, CA 94133
sights.w: The historic Italian fishing port turned waterfront district; walk-up crab and clam-chowder stands line Jefferson Street, and the iconic 1968 crab-wheel sign marks its heart at Taylor and Jefferson.

sights.address: Beach St & The Embarcadero, San Francisco, CA 94133
sights.w: A 45-acre waterfront complex of shops and restaurants best known for the wild California sea lions that have hauled out on K-Dock since 1990, barking and jockeying for space for free.

sights.address: 1 Telegraph Hill Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94133
sights.w: The 210-ft fluted tower atop Telegraph Hill, wrapped inside with free 1934 WPA Depression-era murals of California life; climb the flower-lined wooden Filbert Steps up to it for 360-degree bay views.
sights.k: Ground-floor murals free; elevator to the observation deck about $10.

sights.address: Lombard St between Hyde St & Leavenworth St, San Francisco, CA 94109
sights.w: The one-way brick block on Russian Hill with eight hairpin turns added in 1922 to tame the grade, lined with hydrangea beds; free to walk down the side stairs or drive one-way eastbound.
sights.k: GPS to 1070 Lombard St. Free, open 24/7.

sights.w: The 'Postcard Row' of seven Queen Anne Victorians on Steiner Street, framed against the downtown skyline from Alamo Square Park - among the most photographed houses in America.

sights.address: Dragon Gate, Grant Ave & Bush St, San Francisco, CA 94108
sights.w: The 1970 Dragon Gate at Grant and Bush, a Taiwan gift with guardian lions, is the southern entrance to the oldest Chinatown in North America; Grant Avenue and lantern-strung Ross Alley run north from it.

SF's tallest and most recognizable tower (1972), reopened in 2024 after a $1B restoration; the adjoining half-acre Transamerica Redwood Park, a public grove of coast redwoods with a sculpture, is the free draw.
sights.k: Tower interior is private offices; Redwood Park is the public space.

sights.address: 900 North Point St, San Francisco, CA 94109
sights.w: The 1893 red-brick Ghirardelli chocolate factory, now a landmark open-air complex of shops and restaurants above Aquatic Park; the original Ghirardelli ice-cream and chocolate shop still serves hot-fudge sundaes.

sights.address: Pier 45, Shed A, San Francisco, CA 94133
sights.w: One of the world's largest collections of antique coin-operated arcade machines - 300-plus fortune tellers, player pianos, and the creepy Laffing Sal - free to enter, a quarter or two to play.
sights.k: Free admission; machines take coins. Open daily.

sights.w: A Civil War-era brick coastal fort tucked directly under the south end of the Golden Gate Bridge, with cannon casemates, a spiral staircase, and dramatic bridge-and-bay views; free.
sights.k: Free. Fort interior open Fri-Mon only; grounds Thu-Mon.

sights.w: The national park on Aquatic Park Cove: a free Visitor Center, the streamline-moderne Maritime Museum (900 Beach St), the curved swimming beach and bleachers, and the historic Hyde Street Pier fleet.
sights.k: Hyde Street Pier is closed for the Hyde Street Rebuild and its historic ships are temporarily relocated to Mare Island; Visitor Center, Maritime Museum and Aquatic Park remain open.

sights.address: 83 Marina Green Dr (end of Yacht Rd), San Francisco, CA 94123
sights.w: A wave-activated acoustic sculpture (1986) on a jetty past the Golden Gate Yacht Club, built by Exploratorium artists from salvaged cemetery granite; 25 PVC-and-concrete pipes murmur with the tides.
sights.k: Free, always open; best at high tide.

sights.address: Pier 7, The Embarcadero, San Francisco, CA 94111
sights.w: An 840-ft public promenade pier with antique iron lamp posts and wooden benches jutting into the bay; a favorite for anglers and photographers - the deck lines up straight at the Transamerica Pyramid.
sights.k: Free, open to pedestrians and fishing.
